what_it_does:
The instrument is the thing stage D marks with and stage B certifies. It fixes, before any report exists, what a marker records per report, what counts as agreement, and which fields may carry an arm difference.

In the plan's terms:
- The eleven tests keep plan 52's RAN / NAME ONLY / ABSENT / CANNOT. Plan 52's criterion is kept unchanged for the seven H64 found reliable at 40 of 48 or better (flip 46, pull 45, rival 44, remove 43, hunt 43, patches 41, reverse 40) and sharpened for the four H64's own trap paragraph names (swap 36, poke 35, add a job 35, inside 38). CANNOT is tightened to file 33's three-part form — test named, the document's sentence quoted, a part left unknown — which is the form W3's P4.7 count is made of.
- The three fields H64 struck come back with written rules: shape is no longer judged but derived from seven countable elements (E1..E7); "turned own test" takes the strict of the two readings, because the loose one was Y in 41 of 48 and separated nothing; the same-explanation verdict is presence on one document with the sentence quoted, never a count.
- The three new fields of W3 P3.2: marks_per_part (map from the report's own part label to one of the eight, longest-match, two-mark cells left out and quoted, read by document), pairs_that_pull (pairs of the report's own part labels), rivals_built (stated in its own sentence plus a change that separates, or a statement that none can).
- question_identity: SAME/MOVED on target and what is asked only, with both questions quoted. The range is deliberately excluded, because arm (f) is handed the question with the change list removed and a range comparison would read MOVED on every arm (f) run by construction.
- The modules-opened field is split in two, as W8 part C4 requires: modules_served from the transport's record (the read-out P4.6 is read on) and modules_self_reported marked from the report (the reader's own list). P4.9 is the count of runs where they differ.
- The request-as-sent fields (requests, request_text_saved) are record-sourced and never compared between arms, because requests differ by arm by design; PA.1 is read from the run records.
- Arm (e) gets two fields at two layers: ports_set, written by the harness (and "none set" on the Sonnet control, per B10), and marks_outside_closed_list, the gauge, deliberately kept out of the certified set so P4.4 cannot pass on it by construction.
- Arm (x) gets attributions, one member per numbered part or job the report assigns to a named speaker, read against its own unexchanged arm (a) control and never against the marker's view of who is right.

W8 part B4 does the sorting: three within-step tests (remove, swap, poke) as B4 and W3 P3.5 fix them, eight cross-step, plus remove_in_groups carried apart because B4 names it as cross-step while the eleven-test remove field is within-step. Shape is sorted within-step with the reason written and the falsifier named.
dry_run:
Nothing was sent to any API; no key was read; no network call was made. Four dry runs, all in memory, writing nothing:

1. `python3` importing the harness's own `marks.py` against instrument/criteria.json: loads clean, 32 fields, 18 within-step, 14 cross-step, 25 comparable, 0 example values outside a closed list. marks.py rejects any sort but within-step/cross-step (W8 B4) and it accepted mine, so nothing in A1's code needs changing to read this file.

2. Quote check: every `quote` in the file checked as a verbatim substring of the report it names. 78 verbatim in the named report; 18 carry a `quote_from` key naming a different source (sonnet_agent.py line 55; the run record's own JSON keys `"api_calls": 1` and `"usage_total": {}`; W8 part B10's holder sentence; or derived values with no sentence to quote) and each of those four sources was checked separately and found verbatim. 0 problems.

3. `first_marker.prompt_for(...)` built in memory over these criteria and the F4-m1-r1 report: a 6,232-word, 266-line marking prompt. It asks the marker for all four record-sourced fields, which is ask #1 of the instrument.

4. `agreement.run_agreement(...)` over a synthetic 8-document, 10-arm, 3-repeat marks set built in memory: every prediction stage D reads came out on the right field — PA.2 on the baseline, P4.1 within tolerance, P4.2 on pairs_that_pull under arm (c) at k=3, P4.3 on rivals_built under arm (d), P4.4 on marks_per_part under arm (e), P4.5 on test_remove under arm (f) and on (c') against (c), P4.6 on modules_served under arm (r), PA.3 on attributions under arm (x). A second synthetic run where arm (e) moved nothing but modules_served returned P4.4 holds=True carried by modules_served alone, which is the evidence for ask #2.

One side effect, undone: my imports created `code/__pycache__/` at 12:25 (already excluded by A1's .gitignore). I removed it, leaving A1's folder as I found it.

could_not_settle:
Four things.

1. Whether any criterion carries to a document of a kind neither P3 (a philosophy paper) nor F4 (a novel) belongs to. Every criterion here was tested on twenty-four reports on those two documents, written under skill file 30 by two readers. Under the qualified Derivation 3 (file 11, Part XVI) it is faithful there and, wherever the population admits another reading, unconstrained on A2's twelve new documents under file 33. Stage B on the 96 reports in hand is the first real test; the new corpus is untested by anything until stage C.

2. Whether a marker handed two literal questions side by side reads SAME and MOVED the same way as a marker comparing a report against a stand-in target. No run in the record was handed a question — run.py's framing told each reader to freeze one itself — so the two fitting reports were marked against a stand-in target written down before they were marked. That is a weaker comparison than the one stage D will make, and both files say so.

3. Whether the shape field belongs within-step. It is sorted within-step with the reason written and the falsifier named (arm (d) losing shape while keeping every cross-step field), and B4 forbids re-sorting on the reports that break it, so the answer cannot come before stage C and cannot change this round's instrument if it does.

4. The three asks of the harness are stated, not made. I may not edit A1's code and did not. If A5 does not return them to A1, four fields come back null on every report and P4.4 can be carried by a read-out.
for_the_reviewer:
Press here first, in this order.

1. The four sharpened test criteria are patches, and a patch has a bill. Swap, poke, add a job and look inside now ask more than plan 52 did, so a RAN under this instrument is not the same thing as a RAN in the record, and the two counts must never be laid side by side. Worse, the sharpening could push those four to ABSENT or NAME ONLY almost everywhere, at which point W3's P3.5 would read as the criteria failing when the truth is that the criteria moved. The gauge I have is thin: P3.4's one-second-rewording rule. Ask whether a better gauge exists.

2. The poke rule understates a good report. A report that correctly finds the document affords no poke pair is NAME ONLY. I restated this once already, tightening CANNOT to file 33's three-part form so such a report has a mark to reach, and the record report I use (runs_sonnet5/F4-m2-r1) does not reach it. Ask whether that is the right line or whether the bill is too high.

3. certified_candidate is a key of mine that A1's code does not read. Everything I say about P4.4 not being passable by construction rests on a filter that does not yet exist. I demonstrated the failure rather than asserting it; check the demonstration and then check that the ask reaches A1.

4. I chose the boundaries with W8's predictions in front of me. Two places are marked in the file where that pressure was strongest: excluding the range from question_identity (which protects arm (f)'s result) and keeping the gauges out of the certified set (which makes P4.4 harder, not easier). Look for a third I did not mark.

5. The 39-of-48 threshold. It is mine, not W3's. It is the only number in the striking rule that could have been chosen to save or sink a field. Check it against W3 and W10 and say if it should not exist at all.

6. attributions may not certify. It is a set two markers must match exactly, and it is the sharpest field PA.3 has. If it falls below its threshold in stage B, PA.3 falls back to whatever other certified field moves, which is a much blunter test of W8 A10. Ask whether the member format ('name|label', numbered lists only) is tight enough to agree.

7. Thirty-two fields, 240 reports per reader in stage C, two markers each. Ask whether the instrument is too heavy to run, and if so which field goes. My own answer, if forced: remove_in_groups first (RAN appears nowhere in the record), then shape_elements folded back into shape.
